title: Find the Number of Good Pairs II
summary: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of lengths n and m, and a positive integer k, find the count of pairs (i, j) where nums1[i] is divisible by nums2[j] multiplied by k.
statement: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of lengths n and m, and a positive integer k, find the count of pairs (i, j) where nums1[i] is divisible by nums2[j] multiplied by k.
constraints: Both arrays are nonempty positive-integer arrays and k is positive.
Count index pairs (i,j) satisfying nums1[i] divisible by nums2[j]*k.
Duplicate values correspond to distinct indices and must contribute with their multiplicity.
hints: After dividing nums1[i] by k, every valid nums2[j] is a divisor of the quotient.
Frequency-count nums2 and enumerate paired divisors up to the square root of each divisible nums1 value.
Skip values not divisible by k; for d*q=value/k add both stored frequencies, avoiding a square duplicate.
Divisors are enumerated exactly once per complementary pair, and frequency addition counts every eligible second-array index.
editorial: Divisors are enumerated exactly once per complementary pair, and frequency addition counts every eligible second-array index.

tests.explanation: The five valid index pairs use divisors of 1, 3, and 4 from the second array.
Eight pairs with both second-array values; twelve pairs only with two, totaling three pairs.
